claim: Synopsys, in a 2018 product release, described the traditional RTL-to-GDSII design flow as having clear lines of demarcation between synthesis, place-and-route, and signoff functions.
evidence: "The traditional RTL-to-GDSII design flow has clear lines of demarcation between synthesis, place-and-route, and signoff functions." (Synopsys press release, 19 Mar 2018, para 5)
notes: Fact-check fc-W0-44da: re-typed from fact to reported_claim (vendor marketing release); a simplified split, not an exhaustive list of flow stages.

claim: Google and SkyWater describe the open-source SKY130 PDK release as an experimental preview / alpha release that is not intended for production settings.
evidence: "Google and SkyWater are currently treating the current content as an **experimental preview** / **alpha release**."; "the open source PDK is not intended to be used for production settings at this current time. It *should* be usable for doing test chips" (README, 'Current Status')
notes: Caveat to CLM-0418 found by fact-check fc-W0-44da.

claim: SEMI P39 (OASIS) defines an interchange format for hierarchical integrated-circuit mask layout data and was created, from 2001, as a successor to GDSII Stream, which had been the de facto layout-interchange standard for more than two decades.
evidence: "The purpose of this Specification is to define an interchange and encapsulation format for hierarchical integrated circuit mask layout information."; "In the fall of 2001, SEMI's Data Path Task Force formed a working group to define a successor to the venerable GDSII Stream format, which had served the I.C. industry as a de facto standard for layout interchange for more than two decades." (SEMI P39 abstract)
notes: Fact-check fc-W0-44da: 'succeeded' changed to 'created as a successor'; source does not establish market displacement of GDSII.

claim: SEMI's P39 background states that GDSII Stream was limited by 16-bit and 32-bit integer fields, inefficient geometry representation and high structural overhead, with file sizes in some cases reaching many tens of gigabytes; OASIS was chartered to achieve at least an order-of-magnitude file-size improvement and full 64-bit capability.
evidence: "The old format, limited by 16-bit and 32-bit internal integer fields, by its inefficient representation of cell-native geometric figures, and by high structural overhead ... file sizes were becoming unwieldy, in some cases growing to many tens of gigabytes."; "Achieve at least an order-of-magnitude file size improvement"; "make the new format fully 64-bit capable" (SEMI P39 abstract)
notes: Fact-check fc-W0-44da: adds 'in some cases' and removes the implied causal link between integer width and file size.
